```{=html}
<div class="title-bar">

  <p>Postgame analysis · Week 1, 2026 · Buffalo 36, Houston 31</p>
</div>
```

Houston did the thing offenses are told to do: it got close and finished. Four of its five trips inside Buffalo's 20 ended in touchdowns. Buffalo went one for three.

Buffalo won anyway, because it did not need the red zone. Three of its four touchdown drives never ran a play inside Houston's 20 — they ended on long gains instead. Houston had no touchdown drives like that. And Houston's fifth red-zone trip, the one that could have won the game, ended with a strip-sack fumble with 16 seconds left.

One afternoon, measured through the final whistle. Nothing here says anything about either team's season.

The rest of the box score leaned Houston's way too: a higher success rate (46.6% to 40.4%), more third-down conversions (7 of 16 to 3 of 9), and the ball for 36:17. The full picture is the report below — every number in this story is in it, with the charts behind each one.

## What this is not

- **One game.** A single afternoon is too small to say anything about team quality. Nothing here is a forecast.
- **Red-zone trip** means a drive with at least one snap from the opponent's 20 or closer. Field-goal attempts count; kneel-downs, extra points and two-point tries do not.
- **Win probability** is the feed's model, with no market input.
- **No betting or market prices.** This piece describes one game, nothing more.
